title: Stream jitter oracle and structured-output regression harness
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a deterministic, CI-friendly regression harness that validates end-to-end behavior of: (1) streaming responses under realistic network jitter, (2) tool/function-calling semantics across streaming and non-streaming modes, and (3) structured JSON outputs with robust normalization. The harness should provide an "oracle" layer that fingerprints canonical behavior (token-level traces, tool-call events, and normalized JSON shapes) and flags regressions while being tolerant to non-semantic output variance. This ticket builds the harness, a small reference prompt suite, validators, and CI jobs that gate merges for API/server changes that touch streaming, tool routing, or structured-output formatting.
outcome: A reusable test runner and a canonical reference suite checked into tests/integration/stream-oracle/ with CI jobs on main and canary branches. The runner will produce human-readable diffs, a severity classification (minor/major/regress), and automatic links to failure artifacts. The suite will cover streaming-with-jitter profiles, function-call interleaving, and JSON schema drift detection. Integration should be added to PR templates and the release gating checklist for runtime-1.19.
acceptance_criteria: Test runner executes locally and in CI with deterministic seeding
At least 18 reference prompts covering: short/long context, multi-tool flows, nested JSON outputs, streaming-only cases
Network jitter profiles (latency spikes, packet reordering, slow TTG) simulated and tested in CI
Tool-call event ordering and token-level boundaries asserted in both streaming and non-streaming modes
Structured output validator normalizes whitespace, key ordering, and numeric formatting, and rejects semantic drift beyond tolerance thresholds
PRs that change streaming or tool-call code paths fail CI on regression, with actionable diffs and links
test_matrix: Tooling: single-tool, multi-tool, nested tool calls
Output: scalar text, inline JSON object, JSONL streams (partial chunks)
Network: baseline, jitter-small (50-200ms spikes), jitter-large (200-800ms spikes), partitioned (intermittent drops)
Model variants: long-context optimized, quantized runtime, fallback model variant
Client SDKs: REST curl runner, JS SDK stream harness, python streaming harness
steps: Design oracle format: token trace + event timeline + normalized output snapshot
Implement shim to capture token-level traces in the runtime test fixture
Build a network simulator layer for CI (tc/netem profiles or containerized proxy)
Author 18 reference prompts covering edge cases and store expected fingerprints
Implement structured-output normalizer and schema-aware comparator
Create CI workflows: quick-smoke (fast), nightly-full (heavy jitter profiles), and canary-gate
Instrument failure output: HTML diff, token map visualization, compressed trace artifact upload
Add PR template and docs for writing new oracle prompts and interpreting failures
Run extended runbook with platform and SDK owners and incorporate feedback
notes: We intentionally fingerprint token-level traces rather than raw bytes to avoid spurious regressions from non-deterministic whitespace.
Decision: normalize numeric formatting and sort object keys for JSON comparison. This sacrifices some fidelity for actionable diffs.
Trade-off: nightly-full runs are expensive; CI will gate on quick-smoke and fail fast, nightly job catches subtler regressions.
Potential follow-up: a lightweight fuzzing harness to discover regressions introduced by kernel selection changes. Track as separate ticket if useful.
